R202.note: Deny-by-default JexlSandbox(false) plus a narrow ReportRow allowlist and newInstance/methodCall features off closes the reflection path; the writeFlag=false leaves writes as an empty blacklist (allow-all) on ReportRow, harmless since it has no setters, and the documented comparison/boolean filter grammar still evaluates unchanged.

R203.note: Replacing the source-text string with an arrow callback removes the code-generation step entirely; recordReminder receives the same two arguments and the response is unchanged.

R204.note: Inverting the isAdmin() condition restores exactly the stated contract - admins get Order::all(), non-admins get only their own orders - with no other change.

R205.note: disallow-doctype-decl set on the factory before newDocumentBuilder(), with external-entity features off as defence in depth; DOCTYPE documents now fail into the existing SAXException/400 path, which the write-up states, and DTD-free order XML parses as before.

R206.note: isolated-vm Isolate/Context/Callback/compileScriptSync/runSync usage reads correctly and gives a real heap boundary, but memoryLimit: 8 is isolated-vm's minimum and the full pending-order batch is copied into that heap, so a large legitimate batch could now fail the run where the original had no cap; the write-up presents the cap as guidance without addressing batch size.

R207.note: IsAuthenticated plus owner-scoped get_queryset (so retrieve/destroy 404 for foreign keys) and perform_create forcing owner=request.user closes the gap; dropping the queryset attribute is safe because the router already supplies basename, and all behaviour changes are stated.

R208.note: new File(baseDir, param).getCanonicalFile() with a component-aware Path.startsWith containment check rejects escapes via the existing catch block; fileName echoed in the response is now the canonical path, which is identical to the original for a plain filename under an absolute TESTFILES_DIR.

R209.note: subprocess.run argv with '--' before the host closes both shell and option injection, and stdout=log_file/stderr=STDOUT reproduces the '> log 2>&1' redirect and truncate-on-run semantics; the hardcoded /bin/ping (absent on macOS, present on merged-usr Linux) is a stated assumption.

R210.note: GetFullPath on the combined path then a GetRelativePath check for '..', '..'+separator, or a rooted result rejects absolute, UNC, other-drive and ../ inputs and sibling-prefix directories, and the same fullPath is what ReadAllText opens; legitimate relative filenames resolve to the same file as before.

R211.note: Resolving both REPORTS_DIR and the joined candidate then is_relative_to() rejects absolute overrides and ../ traversal with the checked variable being the one opened; the only other change is missing/non-regular files now returning 404 instead of an unhandled 500, which the write-up records.

R212.note: jwt.decode with the key and an explicit algorithms allowlist restores signature, exp/nbf/iat checks and maps InvalidTokenError to the existing 401; the HS256 choice and the JWT_SECRET env var that must match the issuer (failing startup if absent) are stated plainly as required configuration.

R213.note: Removing exec() in favour of a fixed MIGRATIONS dispatch table is the correct shape for a CPython sink that cannot be sandboxed, but it eliminates the endpoint's stated feature (operator-pasted one-off snippets), renames the request field from code to name, and ships with only a placeholder that raises NotImplementedError, so no legitimate call succeeds until a migration is registered and deployed - the write-up states this trade-off openly.
